deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page: no formulas, symbols, or derivations. It is a short closing remark, in pencil and in German Kurrent, to the philosophical fragment on the previous page (91/92r, 'Allgemeine Sätze über das Wirken'). That page set out general propositions about agency (Wirken). An action of an agent can only affect things capable of the corresponding state. Which things it affects cannot be inferred from the concept of the agent alone. When two things a and b are brought into immediate connection by a single (simple) real ground, a consequence c may be attached to the connectedness itself or to changes in its degree. The 'simplest assumption' is that c is attached to the connectedness.

This page reads, approximately: 'Es ist unnöthig, diese Betrachtung weiter fortzuführen. — Ich bemerke nur noch, dass man den Satz: "Was ein Agens zu bewirken strebt, muss durch den Begriff des Agens bestimmt sein" [anwendet] — diesen Satz aber nicht wie Leibnitz und oder Spinoza auf Wesen mit einer Mannigfaltigkeit von Bestimmungen, sondern auf Realgründe von möglichst grösster Einfachheit anwendet.'

In English: it is unnecessary to pursue this consideration further. I note only that one applies the principle 'what an agent strives to bring about must be determined by the concept of the agent'. One applies it, however, not as Leibniz or Spinoza did, to beings with a manifold of determinations (monads, substance with infinitely many attributes and modes), but to real grounds of the greatest possible simplicity.

The point is methodological. It is a version of the principle of sufficient reason. Riemann restricts it to maximally simple 'Realgründe', in the spirit of Herbart's simple 'Realen'. This fits his self-description as a Herbartian in psychology and epistemology, and his natural-philosophical programme of explaining physical action through simplest elementary laws. It also matches his later notion that only conditions at a point and its immediate neighbourhood should determine action, i.e. contact action. The sentence is grammatically garbled because of revisions: 'dass' is doubled, the phrase 'diesen Satz' resumes 'den Satz', and the verb 'anwendet' appears only once.
errors: No mathematical content to check. The sentence is syntactically incomplete or garbled because of revisions: 'dass' is written twice, and the resumptive 'diesen Satz aber' duplicates 'den Satz'. This is a drafting slip, not a conceptual error.

results.what: Methodological principle: what an agent strives to effect must be determined by its concept, applied to maximally simple real grounds rather than to Leibnizian or Spinozist substances with manifold determinations.
results.modern_name: Principle of sufficient reason; Herbartian ontology of simple 'Realen'
results.usually_credited_to: Leibniz (principle of sufficient reason); J. F. Herbart (simple reals). Riemann's Herbartian natural philosophy is documented in the published 'Fragmente philosophischen Inhalts' (Werke, ed. Weber/Dedekind, 1876).

deep.surprise_reason: This is a brief philosophical remark consistent with Riemann's well-known Herbartian natural-philosophical fragments, which are already published in substance in his collected works. There is no mathematics and nothing novel.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: the reading '— Ich bemerke nur noch, dass' is plausible but uncertain in the image. The words after the dash are hard to read; 'bemerke' is likely, given 'Ich ... nur noch'.
Line 2: the superscript insertion above 'Satz' reads like 'dasselbe' or 'derselbe' and is uncertain. The struck-out mark before 'bewirken' is a small cancelled symbol rather than a word.
Line 3: 'diesen Satz aber nicht wie Leibnitz [durch] und oder Spinoza' is consistent with the image. 'durch' is struck out, and 'und' appears to be replaced by 'oder'.
Line 4: 'einer Mannigfaltigkeit von' is written above, replacing the struck-out 'mannigfaltigen'. 'Bestimmungen, sondern auf Realgründe' is confirmed.
Line 5: 'von möglichst grösster Einfachheit anwendet.' is confirmed.
